title: Bigard's first sax and clarinet night at Mexico's
summary: Luis Russell pushed him to play at Mexico's clarinet night, where his playing made him known, and other clarinetists there were Buster Bailey and Procope.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But they used to have a lot of fun there. Luis Russell had taught me a tune that was being popular around at that time, you know, and I wasn't known at all.

So one night they're going to have saxophone and clarinet nights. So Luis Russell says, "C'mon, I'm going to take you there." I said, "No, not me." He said, "Yes, you are, too." So I says, "Well, okay. Here goes." And I went in there and played a tune. You know, I could play pretty good, boy, and everybody was, "Oh, who's that character? Where did he come from?" Then I began to get known around there and that's how --
Do you remember any of the other saxophonists or clarinetists who were playing there at the same time?
Oh, Buster Bailey, Procope, all them guys that were good clarinetists. They had one guy used to play in a theater. He was a West Indian. I can't think of his name. He was quite a musician, too.
